title: Reduce initial token lag for small-batch long-context requests (customer escalation)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customers reported increased first-token latency (TTFT) and reduced tokens/sec for single-request small-batch traffic with long-context models (32k+). Incidents observed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after last week's runtime-1.22 rollout. Affected flows: low-concurrency interactive chat, some API customers with prompt-engineered long prefixes, and Partners running on Dedicated pools with mixed-batch workloads. AtlasData opened a high-severity escalation citing production errors and visible UX regressions. This ticket coordinates triage, immediate mitigations, and a tested patch to restore prior TTFT/tokens/sec characteristics without increasing overall cost by a large margin.
root_cause_summary: Regression introduced in kernel selection heuristics + scheduler preemption change in runtime-1.22: heuristics started favoring large-stride kernels for batched workloads which performs poorly for single-request small batches with large KV contexts. Scheduler preemption added to improve throughput under high-load inadvertently caused frequent context switches for small-batch long-context shards, amplifying latency. Combined effect: increased TTFT by 60-200ms for affected requests and throughput drops for tokens/sec on interactive flows.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Canary rollback of the new kernel-selection heuristic on 5% of edge hosts for AtlasData traffic. 2) Bypass scheduler preemption for requests with 'low_concurrency_hint' and long-context flag set. 3) Apply temporary priority queue for first-token on small-batch requests to reduce context-switch latency. 4) Notify impacted customers with ETA and mitigation steps.
long_term_fix_plan: 1) Retune kernel selector scoring to include small-batch long-context penalty and add explicit test vectors. 2) Avoid scheduler preemption for NVLink-bound contexts when estimated KV-cache hit probability is high. 3) Add unit/integration tests that synthesize low-concurrency long-context workloads and assert TTFT and tokens/sec thresholds. 4) Improve telemetry (prefix/tail split metrics) and an automated alert for >30% TTFT regression per model-release. 5) Backfill regression test into CI and add a 'first-token' smoke test to the canary pipeline.

qa_and_test_plan: Add synthetic scenarios to CI: single-request small-batch with 32k/64k contexts across models (gpt-like, long-context variants). Thresholds: TTFT <= baseline + 40ms, tokens/sec within 95% of baseline for burst workloads. Add canary smoke that runs 1k requests/hour per canary host for 72 hours.
